steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: A stimulus is the starting point or inspiration for creating a dance

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: There are five main types of stimulus: visual, auditory, kinaesthetic, ideational and literary

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: A visual stimulus is something you see — a painting, photograph, sculpture or film

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: An auditory stimulus is something you hear — music, natural sounds, spoken word or silence

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: Name the five types of stimulus used in dance choreography. | Q: Give an example of a visual stimulus and explain how it could inspire movement. | Q: How does an ideational stimulus differ from a literary stimulus?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Visual, auditory, kinaesthetic, ideational and literary. | A painting of a stormy sea could inspire swirling, expansive movements with sudden changes in dynamics to represent crashing waves. | An ideational stimulus is a concept or theme (e.g. loneliness), whereas a literary stimulus is based on specific words (e.g. a poem about loneliness).

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always name the specific type of stimulus in exam answers — visual, auditory, kinaesthetic, ideational or literary When describing a stimulus, give a concrete example and link it to the movement it inspired Remember that one type of stimulus can lead to many different choreographic outcomes In NEA tasks, clearly state your stimulus type and explain why you chose it For professional works questions, identify the choreographer's stimulus and how it shaped the piece
